title: Agentic Classification Capstone
summary: After this intermediate-level module, learners can determine whether a source correction has enough evidence to proceed and identify the information still needed when the changed source and affected claims are UNKNOWN.
objectives: Determine whether a source-correction record identifies the changed source, its replacement, and the content affected by the change.
Distinguish an authoritative but general source from a verified replacement for a module-specific citation.
Identify the evidence required before modifying learning content without rewriting unaffected material.

sections.title: Correction scope
paragraphs: This is an intermediate-level review of a blocked source correction. It assumes only that the learner can compare a claim with the evidence offered for it. No prior catalogue module is required.

A focused correction requires the existing module, the identity and former location of the changed citation, a verified replacement source, and a mapping from that source to the exact claims it supports. These items allow an editor to correct affected material while leaving unaffected material unchanged.

sections.title: What changed
paragraphs: The cited item supplied for this update is content/modules/agentic-ai-literacy/agentic-classification-capstone.json, described as having an unregistered publisher and never having been verified. Which external citation moved or passed its review cadence is UNKNOWN because no source title, former URL, publisher, replacement URL, or prior verification record was supplied.

What content the source change affected is also UNKNOWN. The existing module was not supplied, so its instructional claims, objectives, sections, questions, explanations, and source mappings cannot be compared with a replacement source. No claim-level correction can therefore be asserted, and no unaffected material can be reproduced as it was.

The correction remains blocked until the verbatim existing file, the changed source entry, evidence of the move or review trigger, a verified replacement, and the affected-content mapping are available. Substituting a merely related source would not establish the intended meaning of agentic classification.
sections.callout: Correction status: the changed citation and its affected content are UNKNOWN, so no instructional claim has been corrected.

sections.title: Why a general source is not a replacement
paragraphs: The National Institute of Standards and Technology describes its Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework as voluntary guidance for organizations that design, develop, deploy, or use artificial intelligence systems. That general scope does not establish that the missing module used the framework's terminology or that the framework defines the intended agentic-classification scheme.

RFC 8259 defines JSON syntax, but it does not define this platform's LearningModule fields or identify the missing instructional source. An authoritative source is suitable only when it directly supports the claim being corrected.

The supplied source checks are dated 2026-08-21, but direct HTTPS resolution was CANNOT VERIFY because network access was unavailable. A future correction must confirm that every selected source resolves over HTTPS and supports the affected text before changing the module.

questions.prompt: What must an editor obtain before making a focused correction to the missing module?
choices: Only a general source about artificial intelligence risk
The existing file, the changed citation, a verified replacement, and a mapping to affected content
questions.explanation: The module states that these items are needed to correct affected claims while preserving unaffected material.

questions.prompt: Which cited external source changed, and what module content did it affect?
choices: Both the source and affected content are UNKNOWN from the supplied evidence
The NIST AI Risk Management Framework changed every section
RFC 8259 changed the module's classification framework
questions.explanation: No external source title, former URL, replacement URL, or affected-content mapping was supplied, so both the changed citation and its effect are UNKNOWN.

questions.prompt: Why is the NIST AI Risk Management Framework not established as a replacement citation here?
choices: It is general guidance and no evidence connects its terminology to the missing module's intended classification framework
Authoritative sources must never be used in learning modules
A replacement citation does not need to support the affected claim
questions.explanation: The module explains that an authoritative general source is not automatically a valid replacement for a module-specific citation.
